description.narrative: Increase in marketed output among project beneficiaries in Lesotho's smallholder agriculture sector and, to improve the Recipient's capacity to respond promptly and effectively to an Eligible Crisis or Emergency.

The objective of the Smallholder Agriculture Development Project is to increase marketed output among project beneficiaries in Lesotho's smallholder agriculture sector. There are three components to the project. The first component is increasing agricultural market opportunities. This component support Lesotho's emerging agricultural businesses to contribute to increased commercialization of the agriculture sector. The second component is increasing market oriented smallholder production. This component support small-scale farmers in their efforts to increase production of marketable commodities and respond more readily to market requirements, to help motivated semi-subsistence producers to improve the productivity of their agricultural activities and become more market-oriented, and to address natural resource management concerns. The third component is project management. this component manage and use resources in accordance with the project's objectives and procedures.

title.narrative: Number of CGP projects completed that are commercially viable.

comment.narrative: <p>Overachieved. based on the final Project Impact Assessment findings, out of total 787 CGPs awarded, 193 CGPs are operational and making a profit. </p>

title.narrative: Client days of training provided under the Agriculture Investment Plan

comment.narrative: <p><strong>Overachieved. </strong>The target value was reduced through restructuring to reflect reduced targets for AIP subprojectswhich consisted of farmer groups and required higher numbers of training days. The target value for AIP subprojects was reduced due to lack of interest amongst smallholders in working together through farmer groups.  </p>

<p><strong>Target for total direct beneficiaries achieved at 102%</strong>. Original target (66,000) assumed higher numbers of AIP subprojects which supported smallholder farmer groups. Due to lack of interest amongst to work in groups, designed funds were reallocated to CGP which supported largely individual family-based enterprises and farms as well as farm associations. Additionally, CERC was added. The target number of beneficiaries was therefore revised to 77,000 to include around 54,000 persons benefitting from non-CERC interventions and 21,000 persons from CERC activities. Project benefitted 78,501 persons, of which 55,361 persons through non-CERC and 23,140 persons through CERC interventions.</p>
<p><strong>Target for shares of female beneficiaries was largely achieved with mixed results for CERC and non-CERC interventions.</strong> Appraisal target of 50% considered only non-CERC interventions such as CGP and AIP. Target for these non-CERC interventions was achieved at 51%. CERC interventions aimed to support eligible affected beneficiaries regardless of gender. The overall project-level target was not updated to reflect the latter factor, however. As such lesser share of female beneficiaries under CERC resulted in 48% of achievement at the overall project level.</p>

title.narrative: Client days of training provided under the Competitive Grants Program Component

comment.narrative: <p>Overachieved. Based on the project field data, total of 79,006 days of training was delivered by the project. The target value for this indicator was increased from initial 11,200 to 60,000 during the October 2016 restructuring. </p>

title.narrative: Targeted beneficiaries satisfied with improved performance of agricultural service providers

comment.narrative: <p>Overachieved based on the findings of the project final Impact Assessment. </p>

title.narrative: Targeted beneficiaries who have adopted improved production technologies / farming practices in targeted areas

comment.narrative: <p><strong>Overachieved</strong>. The target was formally restructured in 2016 to reflect reallocation of funds from AIPs to CGP subprojects. The actual value represents adoption of improved farming technologies and practices by horticulture enterprises only. Theappraisal and restructuring documents do not provide description of how this indicator should be measured. The project monitored only the horticulture enterprises. It should be noted that adoption of improved technologies and farming practices (improved breed, protected animal sheds, animal feeding practices) was high also amongst livestock enterprises.</p>

title.narrative: Farmers and traders in project districts who use public market information

comment.narrative: <p><strong>Not achieved</strong>. Development of public market information system was delayed. It became operational only in 2019 which explains non-achievement of the target.</p>
